title: Playing a powwow on a South Dakota reservation with Bronson
summary: Bronson's band, with Lester, played three days for a powwow in Rapid City to 2,000 or 3,000 people a night, about 1928-29.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: That reminds me of something else. Let me just jump forward a second here. You were talking about with Art Bronson, you and Lester both played at an Indian reservation.
Yeah.
Talk a little bit about that. You said that was a South Dakota Indian reservation.

Rapid City, South Dakota. We went up there... Bronson got a booking up there for... See, when you play out in South Dakota, the people hear you. Like you play a dance. A dance promoter will come where you're playing to hear the band, so he can book you to come to play for his place, as soon as you have an open date. You didn't have no booking agent or nothing; that's where they got in contact. So this guy came and asked Bronson for a date. Said he was going to have a powwow and everything out there. So we went out there and played. Les was with the band. That was in Rapid City, South Dakota.
How many people came out there? That was just one gig, right? One day?
No. We played about three days.
How many people showed up?
Phillips - 124
Each night.
Yeah.
What year was this?
Must have been in about '28 or '29.
During Lester's first stay with the band.
Yeah, all of us. That was the first band.
The first time he was in the band.
Yeah.
What was the reaction of the people like?

Oh, everybody liked music, you know. They was hip to music. You'd play something so you can move around. That's what the people wanted. You'd play some blues. Blues was pretty famous in those days, you know.
How was the Blues doing with the Indians? Were the Indians into the Blues?

Yeah, they was into everything. See, they was right there... They'd hear everything. They was here in the States. You know what I mean? It wasn't like coming from another country. But they knew what was going on. It's like you take Cher. Cher was an Indian. She was down with all that's happening in music. She grew up on a reservation out there in Arizona.
[PAUSE]
One final question about the Young group is about people
Phillips - 125
sharing the bill with them. You said that...
Nobody.
They had the whole bill to themselves.
He had the whole show. His show would last about an hour-and-a-half. See, that's long enough for a show. About an hour-and-a-half or an hour and twenty minutes or something like that.
All right. We'll pick it up again tomorrow.
[PAUSE]
